title: Maximum Number of Visible Points
summary: Given an array of points, an integer angle, and a fixed position, determine the maximum number of points you can see from that position by rotating within the specified angle range.
statement: Given an array of points, an integer angle, and a fixed position, determine the maximum number of points you can see from that position by rotating within the specified angle range. You cannot move from your position but can rotate to see points within your field of view, which is defined as the range [d - angle/2, d + angle/2] where d is the rotation angle. Points at your position are always visible, and points do not obstruct your view.
constraints: There are 1 through 100000 points; the observer stays at location and may face any direction.
A point is visible when its direction lies in a closed viewing sector of angle degrees; points at location are always visible.
hints: Convert every noncoincident point to a polar direction.
Sort angles, duplicate them plus 2π, and find the longest window within the viewing width.
Advance a left pointer whenever the angular difference exceeds the closed sector width.
Duplicating directions linearizes sectors crossing zero; coincident points add to every orientation.
editorial: Duplicating directions linearizes sectors crossing zero; coincident points add to every orientation.

tests.explanation: Facing northeast with a ninety-degree view includes all three directions.
The point at the observer is always visible, and the best narrow sector contains two more points.
